summary: Piney Point Light on the Potomac in St. Mary's County, Maryland: a brick tower lit 1836, unstaffed from 1964, now a county museum and park.

light.focal_note: NRHP focal plane 34 ft above the base; the archive gives 35 ft above mean high water

lens.note: Fifth-order Fresnel lens installed 1855 (LighthouseFriends) or 1856 (archive); a replica is displayed in the museum lantern room

structures.note: NRHP: 30 ft; LighthouseFriends: 26 ft; directory: 35 ft
Second story added in 1884 (LighthouseFriends); NRHP describes a brick house with a frame ell

access.note: Museum and grounds open; tower open in season (see visit).

visit.note: Tower hours differ by source: LighthouseFriends says in season; the directory says daily except some holidays. Check before visiting.

events.note: Brick conical tower and keeper's quarters; NRHP: the first lighthouse built on the Potomac
First lit in September 1836 (LighthouseFriends)
Fifth-order Fresnel lens, 5 June 1855 per LighthouseFriends; the archive gives 1856
Thirty-foot wooden fog bell tower (March 1880)
Second story added to the keeper's house
New model fifth-order lamps installed (Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1900)
Keeper Henry C. Wingate commended for helping a schooner aground (date of the help not given)
Keeper William Yeatman commended for anchoring a power canoe on 2 August 1921
Keeper William Yeatman helped an injured man, 2 February 1926
Beacon and fog horn to be run by electricity (Evening Star, 7 December 1931)
Keeper William Yeatman transferred to Point Lookout as an assistant keeper
Storm: water covered the station grounds; fog-signal apparatus put out of commission and damaged
Reed horn replaced the bell
Hurricane Hazel heavily damaged the bell tower, which was then torn down
Discontinued in 1964 (NRHP, archive, directory); LighthouseFriends gives 1 November 1963
Federal government deeded the property to St. Mary's County; Department of Recreation and Parks; museum group took over operation
Lighthouse opened to the public in May 2002
Hurricane Isabel flooded the museum building (a former Coast Guard cottage)
Replica of the fifth-order lens installed in a lantern room at the museum
Congress allocated $1.9 million to restore and protect the shoreline

notes_for_editor: Method: NRHP data sheet (NRIS 76002171, short form), US Lighthouse Society archive place and roster, LighthouseFriends (facts only, paraphrased), Light-House Board 1900 (scan page 114), Lighthouse Service Bulletins 1913, 1921, 1926 and 1933 (PDF pages), the Evening Star of 7 December 1931 (Chronicling America, p. 26), and Rowlett's Maryland directory. Conflicts left open: tower height (NRHP 30 ft, LighthouseFriends 26 ft, archive 30 ft base to lantern, directory 35 ft total); lens year (LighthouseFriends 5 June 1855, archive 1856); discontinuance (LighthouseFriends 1 November 1963, NRHP, archive and directory 1964); ownership (LighthouseFriends visitor note says the National Park Service owns the site, while the archive and directory say St. Mary's County); Charlotte Suter's years (archive 1844-1846, LighthouseFriends 1845-1846). The presidential-retreat claim comes from LighthouseFriends about the point; the directory says the claim for the light station is wrong. The story keeps the two apart. LighthouseFriends' 1928 account of the keeper's day is its transcription of an unidentified 1928 source; a Chronicling America search did not find it, so the story paraphrases it and quotes only one line. The Yeatman link to Point Lookout rests on the Evening Star's 'Capt. William Yeatman' and LighthouseFriends' 'William Yeatman, Jr.'. The 1933 Bulletin item is undated in its text; the story gives the year only. The 1913 commendation has no date of service in the Bulletin text. Hurricane Hazel (1954) rests on LighthouseFriends alone. The Coast Guard personnel of 1959-1963 are in the roster as the archive prints them, with no role, and are not named in the story. Hours: the directory and LighthouseFriends disagree on tower opening; the story says check before visiting. Checked against the sources: the 1921 and 1926 Bulletin passages (page images) and the Evening Star page 26 (7 December 1931) read as stated; the 1913 and 1933 Bulletin passages read as stated in the OCR text (the 1933 storm passage sits in the York Spit damage article); the 1900 Board report (scan p. 114) is for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1900. Disagreements now stated in the story: discontinuance 1963 (LighthouseFriends) or 1964 (NRHP, archive, directory); tower height 26 ft (LighthouseFriends), 30 ft (NRHP) and 35 ft (directory); Suter's term 1844 (archive) or 1845 (LighthouseFriends); ownership by the National Park Service (LighthouseFriends visitor notes) against St. Mary's County (archive, directory, LighthouseFriends' own history); tower hours (LighthouseFriends against the directory). LighthouseFriends' own wording is paraphrased, with the 1928 keeper's account and the 1876 and 1837 texts kept as quotations.
